defects: Pace fails the measured bar: the longest shot is 5.0s and the median is 2.5s. Three of the 14 seconds are nearly static, and the 'swell' line-field shot and the closing title card overstay.

The hairline wave fields (the 'swell' and 'shore' shots) only drift a few pixels in 1/6 s. The lines carry no weight or easing, and the motion reads as a looping procedural noise field, not a wave building.

Every scene uses the same text entry: mono metadata typed out character by character ('WAVELENGTH 3' → '306 M', 'TH' → 'THE WA') plus a fade-up serif line. The idea is repeated five times with no variation.
The underwater shot's headline enters with a heavy vertical blur and smear (pair 2). It reads as a default text-animator preset, and the letterforms are illegible for several frames.
The orbit-diagram dots advance at a near-constant angular speed. They are clean, but they don't track the light and particulate motion of the underwater plate behind them.
The orange accent line in the sunset shot sits on top of the photoreal water with no depth, lighting or motion relationship to it. It looks like a 2D layer composited over the plate.
At 100%, the crossing hairlines in the crop shift colour slightly along their length, and the dense convergence zones show faint stair-stepping and moiré where lines overlap.
In the soundtrack, the high-frequency ceiling jumps in hard steps (about 12k → 16k → 19k Hz at 2.6s, 5.0s and 7.0s). These look like filtered noise beds switched on and off, not mixed transitions.
The riser from 8 to 10.1s is a textbook white-noise sweep that hard-cuts to silence-level content. It drives the 10s hit, but it is the only real dynamic gesture.
The spectrogram shows few sustained tonal partials. The low band is a static drone with almost no melodic or harmonic movement, which suggests thin generated pads over noise layers.
The bed cuts off abruptly at about 12.8s, and the end tail is very sparse. There is no designed sound under the title card, apart from a single tick at about 14s.
gaps: Choreography and transitions. Top studio work would carry one continuous transformation (wind → line → swell → orbit → breaking wave) through morphs and match-cuts. Here, scenes crossfade between unrelated treatments: a vector line field, a photoreal ocean and an underwater plate. The wave fields also lack mass and anticipation, and the shore-break moment never actually breaks.

Sound design and score. Top work would have layered, produced water foley, a real musical arc and a hit landing on each cut. Here there are stepped noise beds, one stock riser and a static drone, synced to picture only at about 10s and 12.8s.

Finish and typographic system. Text animation is one repeated preset (typewriter mono plus blur-in serif), the vector and photoreal looks never unify, and the hairline renders show moiré and stepping. Best-in-class work would need bespoke type motion per beat and cleaner line rendering.
